speaker_role: independent scholarship consultant/coach (Josyn/Jocelyn Pearson, founder of 'The Scholarship System')
commercial_incentive: Strong — repeatedly promotes a free webinar funnel to sell paid scholarship coaching; cites having helped families secure $15M+
key_insights: FAFSA is free, opens October 1 annually, and must be resubmitted every year starting senior fall through college graduation; it unlocks Pell grants, work-study, and federal student loans

CSS Profile is a separate, more detailed College Board form used by roughly 400 institutions (mostly private/selective, some public) to determine institutional (school-funded) aid, asking about items like home equity, retirement savings, and medical/private-school expenses
CSS Profile costs about $25 for the first school and $16 per additional school, but is free for domestic families with income under $100,000
Students only need to submit CSS Profile if a specific target school requires it, but should always submit FAFSA regardless; requirements must be checked on each school's financial aid site
Admissions deadlines, scholarship application deadlines, and financial aid form deadlines can all differ from each other and must be tracked separately
A FAFSA appeal is possible if the calculated results don't reflect a family's real financial circumstances
Recommends filing early (within the first month or two after October 1), staying organized with a school checklist, gathering tax/financial documents in advance, and carefully checking for errors
specific_numbers_or_facts: CSS Profile fee: ~$25 for first school, ~$16 per additional school; free for families under $100,000 income (per speaker)
About 400 institutions require CSS Profile (per speaker)
Anecdote: a student missed the FAFSA deadline and lost eligibility for about $17,000/year (~$80,000 over four years) in institutional aid, with no exception granted despite appeals (per speaker)
notable_or_distinctive: The cautionary real-world example of a student losing roughly $80,000 in aid over four years due to a single missed FAFSA deadline is a distinctive, concrete illustration of deadline risk.
reliability_notes: Persistent promotional framing toward a paid webinar/coaching funnel; specific dollar figures and institution counts are stated without citing a source; the deadline anecdote is a single unverifiable case.
